verdicts.claim: [9] The pooling feature is NOT config/ini-drivable; there is no injection-free ini fix.
verdicts.reasoning: The composition holds, and the structural argument is actually tighter than the agent's five-part composition. [M] from my own re-read of 0x56363F0: the slot-90 override's ONLY data input is the single byte `[GameState+0x898]` — the Super call folds to `mov al,1; ret` (unconditional), and every other step (0x12C7260 result non-null, [X+0x258] non-null, the 0x12C7DD0 type check against ALokiGameState::StaticClass, [rbx] non-null) is a presence/type guard that can only make the answer FALSE, never TRUE. So config-drivability of the whole feature reduces to the flags on exactly one property, and those are measured non-config (claim 4f). Supporting [M]: the struct has 0 UPROPERTIES and no UHT consumer (claims 1,2 with a positive control); both manager UCLASSes are CLASS_Intrinsic with a superclass chain terminating at UObject, so no CLASS_Config is inherited (claim 3, chain walked by me); ALokiGameState has 0 of 155 config properties despite CLASS_Config|config=Game (claim 5, independently walked); no enable cvar/ini literal exists in the subsystem (claim 7, sweep broadened by me). UE's GConfig binds only CPF_Config/CPF_GlobalConfig properties, so no section or key in the user Engine.ini/Game.ini can reach the gate. ⚠ SCOPE, stated so it is not over-read: this is a claim about the INI/CVAR channel only. It does not exclude other injection-free routes (e.g. a different GameState/game-mode class whose CDO ships the flag TRUE — note BP_LokiGameState, BP_LokiGameStateRounds and BP_LokiGameState_Battlefield do NOT serialize the property and therefore inherit the C++ default TRUE), and it says nothing about a DATA poke at GameState+0x898, which claim 4 makes trivially targetable.

summary:
Re-ran every command against the images. 8 of 9 claims CONFIRMED; 1 DOWNGRADE.

**The one real defect — [8]:** bEnablePooling's SetBitFunc is `0x03368BF0` = `mov byte ptr [rcx+0x2d3],1; ret`, NOT the cited `0x03368BE0` / `[rcx+0x2d2]`. That address belongs to the PRECEDING record `bDebugTarget` (0x07F21120). Proof: `findptr 0x3368BE0` -> .rdata 0x07F21158 = 0x07F21120+0x38, while bEnablePooling's record is 0x07F21160 and its +0x38 slot is 0x07F21198 (`findptr 0x3368BF0`, multiplicity 1). An off-by-one-record read — a byte string printed next to an address it did not come from. The claim's conclusion (no CPF_Config, it's an AssetRegistry tag on AActor, SizeOfOuter 0x390, consumer 0x3359D20) is otherwise fully reproduced.

**Gaps in the agent's method that I closed (results survived all three):**
- [3] The compiled-in-flag test is incomplete on its own, because CLASS_Config is an INHERITED flag. I walked the chain: ULokiActorPoolManager -> UActorPoolManager -> UObject (name arg 0x76E5EFA 'Object', /Script/CoreUObject, InSize 0x30). Nothing config is inherited, so the conclusion holds.
- [2] The agent asserted, without demonstrating, that FStructPropertyParams stores one of those pointers. I built the positive control: it is specifically the Z_Construct at record+0x38 — record 0x07DDDC20 ('Pools') stores ActorPool's Z_Construct 0x32A5530 there, and findptr finds it in all three images. PrimingConfig's Z_Construct 0x32ABB70 has 0 refs in s129, merged2 AND tutorial-hero.
- [6] 'rdi == this' across a 0x448-byte span was unchecked. A capstone reg-access scan over 0x5676AC8..0x5676F17 shows exactly ONE write to rdi in the whole range (the `mov rdi,rcx` itself).
- [1] I calibrated the FStructParams uint16 pair in both directions: sibling 'ActorPool' reads `02 00 18 00`, its array verifiably holds exactly 2 entries, and its own structops writes size 0x18 / align 8.

**Traps I hit that others will hit:**
- Walking ALokiGameState's PropertyArray unbounded over-runs to 157 entries; indices 155/156 are adjacent FClassParams fields whose garbage 'flags' (0x4803602609158d48 / 0x48035dd989158d48) BOTH test true for CPF_GlobalConfig. The real array is exactly 155, terminating at 0x8984C78 = FClassParams+0x18. Bounded walk: CPF_Config 0, CPF_GlobalConfig 0.
- `strxref find "(?i)pool"` SATURATES at 200 matches. I re-ran with narrow regexes that do not saturate: `(?i)pooling` 18, `(?i)priming` 22, `(?i)poolable` 16, all enumerated. Only dotted cvar-shaped names in reach are `Pooling.PrimingFrameBudget` (a budget) and `pcg.RuntimeGeneration.EnablePooling` (a different subsystem).
- Hand arithmetic on rel32 leas gave me a wrong class-name RVA ('etTurretRoot'); machine recomputation gave 0x886F322 = 'LokiActorPoolManager'. Every lea target in this review is machine-computed.

**Non-discriminating evidence flagged inside [0]:** `vtables.py classes "Priming" -> 0` proves nothing — a UScriptStruct never gets a class vtable, so 0 is expected either way. The claim survives on better evidence I dug out: the registration record at .rdata 0x07DDDE80 carries a **CreateCppStructOps** slot (0x32A5590) in the second field, a field FClassRegisterCompiledInInfo does not have.

**Coverage/scope notes:** the '.text-wide exactly ONE site' halves of [4a]/[4c] are lower bounds (52.9-54.9 % decrypted) though I reproduced them in all three images; the identifications do not depend on uniqueness. The .rdata-based absences in [2]/[7] are NOT coverage-limited — I re-measured .rdata at 9,085 pages with 33 all-zero, and .rdata is not demand-decrypted. [9]'s conclusion is about the INI/CVAR channel only; it does not exclude a data poke at GameState+0x898, nor the fact that BP_LokiGameState / BP_LokiGameStateRounds / BP_LokiGameState_Battlefield do not serialize the flag and so inherit the C++ default TRUE.

**Incidental findings, both checked and both non-config:** `bCanPrimeOnServer` (AActor, +0x2d4, flags 0x0020080000010001) and `DeferActorPoolClassLoading` (record 0x0887A9A0, flags = NativeAccessPublic only).
